lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Maple Leafs have reached that late-camp stage where the games matter less than the sorting hat - who stays, who goes, and who looks ready when the bell rings. The most telling development was the visit to the Matthew Mayich family in Arizona, a human moment that cut through the usual preseason churn. Toronto is 5 points behind in the standings, riding a W2 streak after taking both games from Ottawa 6-1 and 4-2, and the mood now is less about box scores than roster shape. Steven Lorentz clearing waivers and the new faces settling into the lineup are the quiet but real stories. Auston Matthews' crew is already working through chemistry and roles. Next comes Tuesday's meeting with Montreal - the last clean test before opening night, and the place where camp talk turns into line combinations.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season has been drained to its final, sober innings - nothing left but a clean handoff and a hard look in the mirror. The Blue Jays fell 5-1 to the Reds on Saturday, dropping to 78-83 and 5th in the AL East, and now they turn to Sunday's 3:07 p.m. finale with Max Scherzer taking the ball while his future hangs in the air. Scherzer has said he'll decide later this offseason whether to keep pitching, a fitting note for a club that has spent too much of the year chasing answers. The youngsters are already arriving: Brett Bateman has earned a look, Sean Keys has been in the mix, and Kazuma Okamoto has been one of the few steady bats. What matters now is the audition - and the offseason, when Toronto must fix the rotation and find more teeth in the lineup.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Training camp has a way of stripping away the noise and exposing the load-bearing beam - and in Toronto, that beam is Scottie Barnes. Scottie Barnes as the linchpin of this roster is the right headline because everything else is still being sorted: Darko Rajaković's rotations, the shape of the frontcourt, and whether the new pieces can keep the floor open enough for Barnes to bully the middle. The Raptors are in the clean, awkward part of the calendar - 0.0 points in the standings, no streak, no baggage, just a date with Miami on Sat. 10/3 at 7:00 PM ET and a lot to prove between now and then. Kawhi Leonard's retirement in Toronto only sharpens the sense that this is Barnes's team now. Watch the first preseason minutes and the depth chart behind Barnes - that is where the real argument begins.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The hits keep landing, and they're landing hard - on the scoreboard and the medical chart. Washington's 37-20 loss to Dallas dropped the Commanders to 0-2, fourth in the NFC East, and stretched the skid to four straight; that's no early stumble, that's a team already digging out of a hole. Jayden Daniels' left elbow injury has forced Marcus Mariota into the fire, and the offense suddenly looks like it's pushing a boulder uphill without its best hand on the wheel. The defense, already nicked, has no margin for error. At 1 p.m. against Seattle, the Commanders need sturdier line play, cleaner quarterbacking, and a little backbone. What matters now is whether they can stop the bleeding before September becomes a full-scale rescue job.

article.title: Leafs Face Canadiens on Tuesday
paragraphs: The Blue Jays dropped their finale to the Reds 5-1 last night, and they are back at Rogers Centre this afternoon for a 3:07 p.m. ET start on Sportsnet. That leaves Toronto at 78-83, with Max Scherzer set to take the ball as he weighs what comes next.

For the Leafs, the preseason turns to Tuesday night against the Canadiens at 7 p.m. ET, with a local stop that Sportsnet noted at the Mayich family before Arizona practice adding a softer note to camp. The Raptors are still in training camp and open preseason Oct. 3 against the Heat, while the Commanders host the Seahawks today at 1 p.m. ET on FOX, still looking for their first win after an 0-2 start.
